I finally went to ‘Cooking Goblin Oni’ in Hongdae, and it was a huge success! It was a perfect evening with the atmosphere, taste, and view. 👍

I ordered a variety of signature dishes, and I was satisfied with every single one.
• Seafood Nurungjitang: The hot and cool soup is excellent! I really liked the chewy texture of the crunchy nurungji soaking into the soup.  It’s so generous that it’s perfect as a side dish with drinks!
• Cheese Potato Pancake: Crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, filled with savory cheese! It was a taste that was standard before fusion.
• Highball: Served with a cool and refreshing highball, it enhanced the taste of the food even more. It was a must-have drink to complete a successful evening! 🥂

reviews.author: Seokwon Lee
reviews.text:
We were three foreign women who didn't know much about Korean, and we were so angry that we almost passed out in the store (the store next to the Touch Five building in Hongdae). We only ordered one meal, but they insisted that the next two pots of food were also ordered through our mobile phones. In the end, three people were forced to pay about 200,000 won for five pots of food, but the food we originally ordered was about 90,000 won.
We went on to explain that we have not placed any additional orders on our phones since we placed our order. However, the owner said this was our “mistake” and that we had to pay because the food had already come out of the kitchen. He said that if we had placed an additional order via mobile phone, wouldn't the additional order time and record remain in the system? We could check the CCTV during that time to see if we had placed an order via mobile phone. However, the owner could not confirm the footage of our order at that time on the CCTV and also refused our request to see the order record.
We did not place any additional orders. He claimed to have ordered more food worth almost 100,000 won, but he ended up being so angry after being forced to pay that he barely ate the food and left the store.
It is also understandable that passports are checked upon entry to verify minors. However, this store did not return my passport and kept it. On what legal basis does the store confiscate my passport? This is clearly illegal. Considering the subsequent overcharging incident, I suspect that the very purpose of receiving a passport upon entry was to charge more for food. We plan to take legal action and even report to the media. At that time, I did not see any other Korean customers handing over their ID cards at the store. It's not that it's a waste of money, but it's so unfair to go through something like this as a foreign tourist.
In the end, I even called the police, but the police said, "You must pay now, and then report it to the Korea Consumer Agency. If you don't pay now, it will be illegal." There was no communication at all.
This owner deceived and hard-sold tourists, and his attitude was also very bad. I've only heard about things like touting tourists on the news, but I never imagined something like this would happen this time. This is my first time seeing a store like this in Korea.
Also, the person who once told a foreign tourist, “Foreigners, please leave,” was also an employee of this store. Other foreign tourists have been discussing a lot online that they have experienced a lot of discrimination in this store. Other tourists should refer to this information.

Another amazing thing about ‘Yawn’ is the friendly English speaking staff!! 😭😭 I always chat lightly with the staff, and it makes me feel better every time I go!

Lastly, this cafe menu has my favorite espresso tonic!!! I haven't seen it in any cafe since I came to Korea. But it's my favorite drink in Korea. It makes me want to come here every day. Is there anything better than freshly brewed sparkling coffee on a hot summer day?!😫
